ops.body:
Commit 045650d6 stamped the committed Unreleased section (the Captain Hook.app helper work) as 10.3.0 and renamed the helper cask token to captain-hook; the v10.3.0 tag cuts the first helper release (cask-publish proof). The in-flight verbose-comment-budget + doc-classification work had claimed 10.3.0 in an uncommitted CHANGELOG hunk; that hunk's header was converted to '## [Unreleased]' in the shared working copy (entries untouched, still uncommitted). When that work ships, take 10.4.0 (it removes DOC_PREFIXES/GO_DOC_SIBLINGS exports — arguably minor per the repo's convention) and move the Unreleased section above 10.3.0 if the editor placed it below.
Outcome (2026-07-19): the renumber happened (f5ebe991) and v10.4.0 was tagged by the comment-budget session while the helper leg was still blocked on provisioning profiles — its helper job failed, cask skipped. After the profiles were created (ASC API, runbook aabb893), the v10.4.0 run's failed jobs were re-run: helper signed/notarized/stapled and the captain-hook cask published at 10.4.0. No v10.3.0 tag exists or ever will; the CHANGELOG's 10.3.0 section was folded into 10.4.0.
